headline: Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDA. Why Apple, Broadcom, and Anthropic Could Be Under Pressure
summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) sent stocks sharply higher on Monday morning. NVIDIA shares opened up 34% at about $170, restoring more than $1 trillion of value to shareholders. The NASDAQ rose about 6.75% and the S&P 500 about 4.6%, erasing much of Friday's sell-off. Bleeker focuses on stocks lagging a market where nearly everything is up. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) gained only about 1.7%, and he says a rotation back into AI-adjacent names could pull capital out of the safe-haven stock. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) rose about 6% at the open, trailing the NASDAQ and semiconductor indexes. It fell about 12% Friday on reports that Google was cutting some of its TPU allocation. Anthropic (NASDAQ: ANT) also rose 6%, but its shares have been under pressure since Thursday's IPO, and NVIDIA's backing of open-weight models is a competitive threat. CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 5% at the open, partly on its $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS). Bleeker notes that money that moved into cybersecurity as semiconductors sold off could rotate back. He says to watch for competitive pressure on these names in the coming weeks.

headline: CrowdStrike Shares Fall 10% After a $44 Billion Zscaler Deal Despite an Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance
summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., explains why shares of CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 10% on Monday, November 23, while most tech stocks rallied. The trigger was a proposed acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) for about $44 billion, announced the same morning. The sell-off came despite a strong report. CrowdStrike posted revenue growth of 28.3% against expectations of 23.9%, and EPS of $0.34 against $0.31. It also raised full-year guidance. Bleeker points to the deal instead: Zscaler's wide product line may be hard to integrate into CrowdStrike's platform, and the roughly 34% premium arrives when cybersecurity stocks are richly valued. Zscaler shares rose about 16%, while CrowdStrike is now down 26% from its recent highs. Bleeker lays out both cases. The bull case is that cybersecurity budgets must rise as companies patch systems, with outages at Apple and others as examples. The bear case is that frontier AI models may become the center of cyber defense, which raises questions about what companies like CrowdStrike offer. Expect choppy trading in these shares while investors sort that out.

headline: Palantir Rips 10% to Lead Software Stocks. Cloudflare and ServiceNow Also Join ‘Jensen Rally’
summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA is lifting technology stocks on Monday. The NASDAQ was up more than 7% as of 1:30 p.m. Eastern, after opening with a 3% pre-market gain following Friday's sell-off. Chip stocks as a group rose more than 13%. Software is also higher, but the gains are uneven. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) are each up about 3%, while the IGV software ETF is up 4%. The biggest winners are companies that benefit from sovereign AI and a strong open-weight ecosystem. Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) leads at 10%, and Palantir has been one of the loudest backers of sovereign AI. Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is up roughly 7%, and ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) is up 5%, helped by its control tower software that guides customers between models and agentic workloads. Anthropic is lagging, since Huang has pushed open-weight models that pressure leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Bleeker's takeaway: if Huang keeps backing open weight model makers, Palantir, Cloudflare and ServiceNow, up 5% to 10%, should keep outperforming the 2% to 3% gains in the rest of software.
